notes: A hand-checked starting catalog. Each entry says where it was confirmed (verified: official / third_party / unconfirmed) and when. Program owners change details without notice, so every card links to the official page. Deadlines are shown only when the source published one.

programs.name: NRC IRAP
programs.summary: Funding and an advisor for Canadian SMEs building technology products or services.
programs.amount: Covers part of eligible R&D costs, set project by project (recent calls: up to 80% of eligible staff salaries, 50% of contractor fees)
requirements: Incorporated, for-profit SME in Canada
500 or fewer employees
Innovative, technology-driven product or service
Talk to an Industrial Technology Advisor first

deadline.note: Not listed in the source; contact the NRC for current intake

programs.name: SR&ED tax incentive
programs.summary: Refundable tax credit on qualifying research and development spending.
programs.amount: 35% refundable credit for Canadian-controlled private corporations on spending up to the expenditure limit ($4.5M; a rise to $6M is proposed), 15% above it
requirements: Incorporated and paying Canadian corporate tax
Work that seeks technological advancement and resolves uncertainty
Claim filed with your corporate tax return

deadline.note: Claimed each year with the corporate tax return

programs.name: Ontario Innovation Tax Credit
programs.summary: Refundable Ontario credit on SR&ED spending done in Ontario.
programs.amount: 8% of qualifying Ontario SR&ED spending, on up to $3M (maximum credit $240,000)
requirements: Permanent establishment in Ontario
SR&ED carried out in Ontario
Eligible for the federal SR&ED credit and T661 filed
Limit shrinks once prior-year taxable income passes $500,000

deadline.note: File Schedule 566 with your T2 return

programs.name: CanExport SMEs
programs.summary: Matching funds for export marketing, trade shows, market research and IP in new markets.
programs.amount: $10,000 to $50,000 per project, up to 50% of eligible costs (project value $20,000 to $100,000)
requirements: 3 to 500 full-time employees
$300,000 to $100M annual revenue in Canada
Incorporated, LLP or co-operative with a CRA business number
Matching share paid in cash

deadline.note: 2026-27 guide does not list dates; check the program page for the current intake

programs.name: Canada Small Business Financing Program
programs.org: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
programs.summary: Government-backed loans from banks and credit unions for equipment, leaseholds and property.
programs.amount: Up to $1.15M in total (up to $1M term loans, $150,000 lines of credit)
requirements: Gross annual revenue of $10M or less
Start-ups and existing businesses qualify, farming excluded
You apply at your own bank or credit union, which decides
2% registration fee

deadline.note: Apply to a participating lender any time

programs.name: Futurpreneur startup loan and mentor
programs.summary: A startup loan plus up to two years of one-on-one mentoring for founders aged 18 to 39.
programs.amount: Up to $75,000 combined with BDC, per Futurpreneur's announcement
requirements: Aged 18 to 39 when you apply
Business plan and 24-month cash flow
Pre-startup or startup stage
You must take the loan to be matched with a mentor

deadline.note: Apply any time; the team replies within about 5 to 10 business days

programs.name: Futurpreneur startup program for newcomers
programs.summary: A smaller startup loan and mentor for young newcomers with little Canadian credit history.
programs.amount: Up to $25,000 ($12,500 from Futurpreneur and $12,500 from BDC)
requirements: Aged 18 to 39
In Canada fewer than 60 months
Citizen or permanent resident
Limited or no Canadian credit history
Two character references

deadline.note: Apply any time

programs.name: Black Entrepreneurship Loan Fund
programs.summary: Loans for Black-owned businesses at any stage, delivered through the Black Entrepreneurship Program.
requirements: At least 51% Black ownership
Sole proprietorship or for-profit business
Business plan, financial statements and 2 to 3 year projections
Not open to non-profits

deadline.note: Open continuously, no set deadline

programs.name: DMZ Black Innovation Programs
programs.summary: Programs for Black founders, starting with a 10-week Validator for testing an idea and demand.
programs.amount: Not stated on the page
requirements: Black-founded
Based in the Greater Toronto Area
Idea validation stage for the Validator

deadline.note: A listing shows 'Nov 20' without saying what it is; confirm on the page

programs.name: Indigenous Growth Fund (via Indigenous Financial Institutions)
programs.summary: Capital that Indigenous Financial Institutions lend on to First Nations, Inuit and Metis entrepreneurs.
programs.amount: Set by each Indigenous Financial Institution
requirements: First Nations, Inuit or Metis business owner
Apply through your regional Indigenous Financial Institution, not to the fund directly

deadline.note: Depends on the lender you apply to

programs.name: Women Entrepreneurship Fund
programs.org: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
programs.summary: Non-repayable contributions for women-owned and women-led businesses.
requirements: Women-owned and/or women-led
Fewer than 500 employees
At least 2 years in operation
Two years of financial statements

deadline.note: Not accepting requests now; the page offers a notice when it reopens

programs.name: Communitech Fierce Founders
programs.summary: Cash and coaching for women-identifying and underrepresented tech founders in Waterloo Region.
programs.amount: Uplift: $10,000 cash. Intensive: up to $50,000 on milestones with matching required
requirements: Women-identifying or underrepresented founder leadership
Connection to the Waterloo Region tech ecosystem
MVP or early traction

deadline.note: Rolling cycles; the source lists no dates and is inconsistent on current status

programs.name: ventureLAB Hardware Catalyst Initiative
programs.summary: Up to 24 months of no-equity support, labs and tools for hardware and silicon companies.
programs.amount: No cash; labs, design tools and advisors at no cost, no equity
requirements: Canadian-incorporated hardware or silicon company
Founded within 5 years, under $5M revenue
99 or fewer employees, team of two or more
Southern Ontario presence

deadline.note: Applications are closed; the page describes a review, panel and a 2-month bootcamp

programs.name: Velocity Incubator (University of Waterloo)
programs.summary: Pre-seed incubator with labs, equipment and experienced founders for full-time tech founders.
programs.amount: Not stated
requirements: Founders willing to work on the company full-time
A credible path to solving a very large problem
Open to the public, not only students

deadline.note: Rolling applications, accepted any time

programs.name: OVIN R&D Partnership Fund
programs.summary: Co-funding for Ontario companies developing and testing vehicle and mobility technology.
programs.amount: Stream 1 up to $100,000 over 12 months; Stream 2 up to $1M over 24 months; every OVIN dollar matched at least 2:1
requirements: Incorporated, operating in Ontario, fewer than 500 employees
Working product at readiness level 3 to 9
Automotive or mobility technology
Full proposals by invitation after an expression of interest

deadline.note: Expression of interest, per a third-party summary; confirm on ovinhub.ca

programs.name: Mitacs Accelerate
programs.summary: Put a graduate student or postdoc on your R&D problem with a university supervisor, mostly paid by Mitacs.
programs.amount: $15,000 per 4 to 6 month internship; the company pays from $7,500
requirements: A company, hospital or other partner organization in Canada
A faculty supervisor at a Canadian institution
Partner contribution paid before funds are released
About 6 to 8 weeks of peer review

deadline.note: Not listed on the page; ask a Mitacs advisor

programs.name: Summer Company
programs.summary: Up to $3,000 and coaching for students running their own business over the summer.
programs.amount: Up to $3,000 in two payments
requirements: Aged 15 to 29 and returning to school in the fall
Ontario resident, citizen or permanent resident
Brand-new business, sole proprietor or majority owner
Apply through your local Small Business Advisory Centre

deadline.note: Runs each spring to Labour Day; no date on the guidelines page, apply early

programs.name: Starter Company Plus (Toronto)
programs.org: City of Toronto Small Business Enterprise Centre
programs.summary: A $5,000 micro-grant with business training and three months of mentoring for Toronto founders.
programs.amount: $5,000 plus up to 15 hours of training
requirements: 18 or older, citizen or permanent resident, Toronto resident
Business operating 6 months to 5 years with a business bank account
At least 35 hours a week on the business
You invest 25% of the grant yourself

deadline.note: Applications closed for now; other Ontario cities run their own rounds

programs.name: BMO Launch Me
programs.org: Longo Centre for Entrepreneurship, Humber Polytechnic
programs.summary: Workshops and a pitch competition for Humber students and alumni.
programs.amount: Not confirmed
requirements: Humber students and alumni (per Humber news pages)

deadline.note: The program page was offline when checked; confirm dates with the Longo Centre

programs.name: BDC Capital venture funds
programs.summary: Venture investment in Canadian tech and innovation companies, through funds with different stage and sector focus.
programs.amount: Varies by fund
requirements: Canadian company
Fit with a specific fund's stage and sector
Submit the online intake form; you are contacted only if there is a fit

deadline.note: Intake open continuously

programs.name: Start-up Visa
programs.summary: A route to permanent residence for founders backed by a designated Canadian organization.
programs.amount: Not a funding program
requirements: Support from a designated organization
Innovative business able to create Canadian jobs
